Subject: Cost runway & savings hypotheses — follow-up and next steps

Hi Carla,

Thanks for taking the time today — appreciated the candid run-through of Nebula's constraints. Quick written recap so we have a shared record and clear next steps. Please flag anything I got wrong.

Call highlights / pain: 
- Unpredictable monthly spikes from our eligibility and enrichment flows (peak bursts during credit-check windows).
- Current token spend for your eligibility flow: ~1.2M tokens/day avg with 3–4x spikes; finance says this is blowing past the forecast.
- Latency requirement: sub-400ms p95 for the eligibility endpoint when routed to the primary region.
- Procurement runway: you called out a hard pilot budget (~$120k) for a 90-day proof-of-value.

Initial cost / savings hypotheses (we'll validate in the TCO doc attached):
1) Batch + priority routing — grouping burst requests where possible to reduce per-token overhead (estimate: 20–35% token-cost reduction for batchable portions).
2) Prefix/KV caching for repeated user prompts (sizable wins on eligibility repeat checks; estimate: 10–25% reduction depending on cache hit rate).
3) Model variant + quantization mix — route low-risk checks to a smaller quantized variant; keep high-sensitivity checks on full precision (estimate: 15–30% net cost delta with 'fallback' policy in place).
4) Token budget guardrails — circuit-breaker thresholds and per-route throttles to avoid runaway spend spikes.

Requested confirmation from you:
- Top 3 priorities (you mentioned 1) cost predictability, 2) latency guarantees, 3) auditability). Please confirm or reorder.
- Accepting our proposed pilot scope: 90-day pilot focused on eligibility + enrichment (we'll provide a workload-specified TCO and implementation plan).

Next steps I propose:
1) I will send an updated TCO estimate + pilot scope (attached: redwood-tco-estimate.xlsx, pilot-scope-onepager.pdf) by EOD tomorrow.
2) Sean will own the implementation checklist and runbook; Monica will help with procurement/contract questions.
3) Schedule a 30-minute pilot kickoff (proposed window: week of Jul 6).
4) If procurement is comfortable, we can accept a PO against the pilot scope — I attached a PO template for your finance team to review.

Attachments: redwood-tco-estimate.xlsx (estimates), pilot-scope-onepager.pdf, po-template.docx

Thanks again — happy to hop on a quick call if you want to walk the numbers together.

Best,
Ava Chen
Enterprise Account Executive
Redwood Inference

Ava,

Thanks for the recap — this is the right level of detail. A few clarifications from our side:
- The $120k pilot cap is firm for this fiscal quarter, but we can structure milestone payments tied to deliverables.
- Our eligibility flow is sensitive to latency for customer-facing checks; anything above ~400ms p95 will cause product to fall back to a slower legacy path. So latency is non-negotiable for that route.
- Audit requirements: we need request-level logs and an immutable audit trail for model selection/route decisions for compliance.

Confirming priorities: 1) Latency / reliability, 2) Cost predictability (not just avg savings), 3) Auditability and traceability.

Procurement note: looping in Liam — he is our procurement lead and will coordinate the PO and any contractual redlines. Liam: we expect to have some template language for pilot payment terms; Ava, please share the DocuSign/PO link.
